extra_json: {"definition": "\"Individuals with anomalous trichromacy possess three types of cones, but one of the three types of cones has an abnormal spectral sensitivity compared to normal cones.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Deuteranomaly
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with abnormal M photopigment, such that the absorption spectrum is shifted toward L wavelengths. Affected individuals have difficulties distinguishing between red and green.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Deuteranopia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Complete lack of the M photopigment, which is replaced with the L photopigment. Affected individuals tend to confuse red and green.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Protanopia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Blue and green cones only; no functional red cones.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Iris cyst
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An iris cyst is composed of a single cell layer of epithelium and is filled with fluid.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Iris melanoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Malignant tumor of melanocytes affecting the iris.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_ncarter]"}

name: Iris nevus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A benign brown pigmented area over the iris representing proliferation of melanocyte cells in the stromal layer of the iris. An iris nevus can be flat or occasionally slightly elevated.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_ncarter]"}

name: Lentiglobus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Exaggerated curvature of the lens of the eye, producing an anterior or posterior spherical bulging.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Solitary congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Sharply demarcated hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) that is congenital and of no functional significance.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Multiple congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Unilateral or bilateral small, well-demarcated pigmented lesions localized in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Lesions are dark in the center, with a pale circumference and are mostly located in the periphery.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8727-6592]"}

name: Vitritis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Inflammation of the vitreous body, characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells and protein exudate in the vitreous cavity.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Subretinal exudate
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of retinal exudate located in the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Snowflake vitreoretinal degeneration
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The appearance of yellow/white crystalline-like (hence the name) spots in the retina and thickening of the peripheral part of the vitreous.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_ncarter, PMID:18179896]"}

name: Abnormal spatial orientation of the cardiac segments
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the cardiac segments to other components of the heart.\" []"}

name: Abnormal atrial arrangement
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the atria to other components of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Right atrial isomerism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Right atrial isomerism is characterized by bilateral triangular, morphologically right atrial, appendages, both joining the atrial chamber along a broad front with internal terminal crest.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:3408620]"}

name: Left atrial isomerism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"In left atrial isomerism there is a bilateral small finger-shaped morphologically left atrial appendage joining the atrial chamber along a narrow front without an internal terminal crest.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:3408620]"}

name: Atrial situs inversus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Mirror image atrial arrangement, with morphologic right atrium on the left hand side and morphologic left atrium on the right hand side.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Levotransposition of the great arteries
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a discordance of atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial connections. The anatomy of ccTGA involves systemic venous drainage to the morphologic right atrium (mRA), which is connected via the mitral valve to the morphologic left ventricle (mLV) whose outflow is the pulmonary arterial system. The pulmonary venous drainage arrives at the morphologic left atrium (mLA), which crosses the tricuspid valve into the morphologic right ventricle (mRV) with outflow into the systemic arterial system. In isolation, ccTGA has an in-series circulation without mixing; therefore, the presence or absence of associated defects dictates the patient's clinical presentation.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:21569592, PMID:27777298, PMID:32274202]"}

name: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Crossing of the inflow streams of the two ventricles, due to an apparent twisting of the heart about its long axis.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with superior-inferior ventricles
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with a rare cardiac malformation characterized by the two ventricles lying one above the other instead of side by side.\" [PMID:11789809]"}

name: Superior-inferior ventricles without criss-cross atrioventricular valves
Abnormal connection of the cardiac segments
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A deviance in the normal connections between two cardiac segments.\" [PMID:24876921]"}

name: Abnormal atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the circulatory connection between atria and ventricles.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Absent left sided atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A defect where there is no connection between the left atrium and left ventricle.\" [PMID:7104116]"}

name: Absent right sided atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A defect where there is no connection between the right atrium and right ventricle.\" [PMID:7104116]"}

name: Univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connection
Biventricular heart with straddling right sided atrioventricular valve and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
Right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
Ambiguous atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"With left or right cardiac isomerism in a biventricular, the atrioventricular connections are perforce ambiguous, in that one of the connections is concordant (e.g., right-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic right ventricle) and one of the connections is discordant (e.g., left-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic left ventricle).\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Discordant atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Connection of the right atrium to the left ventricle and of the left atrium to the right ventricle in a biventricular heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:23804932]"}

name: Double inlet atrioventricular connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Double inlet left ventricle
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The condition in which both atria are joined to the left ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually there is a hypoplastic right ventricle, which may be on the opposite side of the heart as usual.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Double inlet right ventricle
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The condition in which both atria are joined to the right ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually, the left ventricle is hypoplastic.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Double inlet to single ventricle of indeterminate morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. The morphology of this ventricle does not allow one to determine if it corresponds to the left or right ventricle.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Double inlet to single ventricle with common atrioventricular orifice
Double inlet to single ventricle with two atrioventricular valves
Mitral atresia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital defect with failure to open of the mitral valve orifice.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Overriding atrioventricular valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An atrioventricular valve that empties into both ventricles. The valve overrides the interventricular septum above a ventricular septum defect.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:7295418]"}

name: Straddling atrioventricular valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anomalous insertion of the chordae tendinae or papillary muscles into the contralateral ventricle in the presence of a ventricular septum defect.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:7295418]"}

name: Abnormal ventriculoarterial connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the circulatory connection between the ventricles and the pulmonary artery and aorta.\" [PMID:15227248, PMID:18805185, PMID:24750982]"}

name: Mitral valve arcade
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anomalous mitral valve arcade is diagnosed based on the following features (1) An adequately sized mitral valve orifice; (2) short, thick, and poorly differentiated chordae with direct union of the papillary muscles to the anterior leaflet; (3) narrow or nearly nonexistent spaces between the abnormal chordae; and (4) greater differentiation of the chordae attached to the posterior papillary muscle.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:20404264]"}

name: Common atrium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Complete absence of the interatrial septum with common atrioventricular valve and two atrioventricular connections.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Cor triatriatum dexter
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital anomaly with partitioning of the right atrium to form a triatrial heart caused by persistence of the right valve of the sinus venosus. Typically, the right atrial partition is due to exaggerated fetal eustachian and thebesian valves, which together form an incomplete septum across the lower part of the atrium. This septum may range from a reticulum to a substantial sheet of tissue.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17948095]"}

name: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An interatrial communication caused by a deficiency of the common wall between the superior vena cava (SVC) and the right-sided pulmonary veins. SVASD is commonly associated with anomalous pulmonary venous connection (APVC) of some or all of the pulmonary veins, which produces additional left-to-right shunting.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:16172274]"}

name: Double orifice mitral valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The left atrio-ventricular connection consists of two anatomically distinct orifices separated by accessory fibrous tissue.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:20851840]"}

name: Cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Cleft in the anterior mitral valve leaflet not associated with an atrioventricular canal defect.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:6829465]"}

name: Parachute mitral valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormality of the mitral valve apparatus, whereby chordae attach to a single papillary muscle or hypoplastic papillary muscles.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Supramitral ring
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital stenotic mitral valvular anomaly with a ring of tissue above the mitral valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Hypoplastic tricuspid valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Congenital defect characterized by underdevelopment of the tricuspid valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Imperforate atrioventricular valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An atrioventricular valve that has failed to open (atretic).\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Imperforate tricuspid valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A tricuspid valve that has failed to open.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:7066117]"}

name: Intermediate atrioventricular canal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and inlet ventricular defect. There is one valve annulus and two valve orifices.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Partial atrioventricular canal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A specific combination of heart defects including a primum atrial septal defect and cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet. There is not an inlet ventricular septal defect present. There are two valve annuluses and two valve orifices.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Transitional atrioventricular canal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and an inlet ventricular septal defect. There are two valve annuli and two valve orifices.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Unbalanced atrioventricular canal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anatomic features of unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) include varying amounts of ventricular hypoplasia, as well as malalignment of the atrioventricular junction. In complete AVSD, the common AV valve can be situated either equally over the right and left ventricles (balanced) or unequally over the ventricles (unbalanced).\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:20837915]"}

name: Short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Double outlet left ventricle
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital defect of heart development characterized by origin of both pulmonary artery and aorta from the morphological left ventricle.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abdominal ectopia cordis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and into the abdomen.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Cervical ectopia cordis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region and without a defect of the sternum.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Thoracocervical ectopia cordis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region with a defect of the superior portion of the sternum.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Thoracic ectopia cordis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Congenital malformation of the thoracic wall with partial or total displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity. This feature is associated with sternal cleft or absence of the sternum.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Thoracoabdominal ectopia cordis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and displacement partially into the abdominal cavity.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19479716]"}

name: Abnormal branching pattern of the aortic arch
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Cervical aortic arch
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The aortic arch extends into the soft tissues of the neck before turning down into to become the descending aorta.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Common origin of the right brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The left common carotid artery has a common origin with the innominate artery.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17138027]"}

name: Double aortic arch
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A conenital abnormality of the aortic arch in which the two embryonic aortc arches form a vascular ring that surrounds the trachea or esophagus and then join to form the descending aorta. Double aortic arch can cause symptoms because of compression of the esophagus (dysphagia, cyanosis while eating) or trachea (stridor).\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:15148283, PMID:15564538]"}

name: Left aortic arch with cervical origin of the right subclavian artery
Left aortic arch with isolated subclavian artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The subclavian artery arises from ductus arteriosus. While the ductus arteriosus is patent its blood supply comes from the ductus, hence from the pulmonary artery. After it closes, the blood supply is retrogradely from the vertebral artery via the circle of Willis.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A patent ductus arteriosus or ductal ligament completes the ring.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Right aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus. The left carotid artery is the first branch, right carotid artery the second branch and right subclavian artery as the third branch.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:12075866]"}

name: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal right subclavian artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Aortic arch crosses the left mainstem bronchus. The first branch is the right carotid artery, the second branch is the left carotid artery, the third branch is the subclavian artery, the fourth branch is the right subclavian artery arising from the posteromedial aspect of the distal aortic arch and continuing posterior to the esophagus to the right hand side of the body.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Left aortic arch with right descending aorta and right ductus arteriosus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The ring may be completed by the ductal ligament.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Right aortic arch with left descending aorta and left ductus arteriosus
Right aortic arch with retroesophageal left subclavian artery
Mesocardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Mesocardia is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal direction of ventricular apex
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex. Left sided is normal.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Rightward direction of ventricular apex
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex towards the right. Left sided is normal.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Midline direction of ventricular apex
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex in the midline. Left sided is normal.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Congenital malformation of the great arteries
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.\" []"}

name: Aortopulmonary window
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital anomaly with an abnormal connection between the aorta and the main pulmonary artery resulting in an aortopulmonary shunt.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Type II truncus arteriosus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with each pulmonary artery arising separate from each other on the posterior or lateral aspect of the truncus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Type III truncus arteriosus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby one of the two pulmonary artery branched does not arise from the common pulmonary trunk, but instead from the ductus arteriosus or directly from the aorta.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Type IV truncus arteriosus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby the aortic arch is hypoplastic or interrupted, and a large patent ductus arteriosus is present.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Interrupted aortic arch
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Non-continuity of the arch of aorta with an atretic point or absent segment.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Interrupted aortic arch type A
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment at the level of the isthmus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Interrupted aortic arch type B
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the left carotid and subclavian arteries.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Interrupted aortic arch type C
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the innominate and left carotid arteries.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Abnormal pulmonary situs morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, which is defined by characteristics such as the number of lobes per lung and the relationship of the pulmonary arteries to their bronchi.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Pulmonary situs inversus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Mirror image arrangement of the mainstem bronchi with the right pulmonary artery posterior to the right upper lobe bronchus and the left pulmonary artery anterior to the left upper lobe bronchus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lungs
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a right lung.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic left lungs
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a left lung.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Abnormality of abdominal situs
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the abdominal situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the abdomen and its organs.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Gerbode ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of ventricular septal defect communicating directly between the left ventricle and right atrium. This is anatomically possible because the normal tricuspid valve is more apically displaced than the mitral valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:19561249]"}

name: Inlet ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A ventricular septal defect that involves the inlet of the right ventricular septum immediately inferior to the AV valve apparatus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:17101870]"}

name: Muscular ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The trabecular septum is the largest part of the interventricular septum. It extends from the membranous septum to the apex and superiorly to the infundibular septum. A defect in the trabecular septum is called muscular VSD if the defect is completely rimmed by muscle.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:17101870]"}

name: Apical muscular ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A muscular ventricular septal defect located at the apex of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Multiple muscular ventricular septal defects
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of muscular ventricular septal defect characterized by the presence of multiple small defects in the ventricular septum.\" [PMID:22718060]"}

name: Scimitar anomaly
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Right pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:16638549]"}

name: Aorto-ventricular tunnel
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.\" [PMID:17922908]"}

name: Congenital defect of the pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A developmental defect of the pericardium with congenital onset.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Total absence of the pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Complete diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"No pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Complete right sided absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"No pericardium is present on the righthand side of the heart. It is a congenital absence of pericardium rather than the result of a pericardectomy.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Partial right sided absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the righthand side of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Complete left sided absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital anomaly with complete lack of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Partial left sided absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Partial diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Lack of a part of the pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Abnormal coronary artery origin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Isolated abnormalities of the coronary artery origins. This may be in associated with other structural heart malformations but not the patterns of complex structural heart malformations which result in abnormal course of the coronary arteries.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Left main coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the left cusp of the aortic valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:27358682]"}

name: Anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Right coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the right cusp of the aortic valve.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Single coronary artery origin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of a single coronary artery ostium from which both coronary arteries arise.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:4547578]"}

name: Coronary artery fistula
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and a heart chamber or another blood vessel.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:20513726]"}

name: Abnormal coronary sinus morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the coronary sinus, which is formed by the union of the great cardiac vein and the left marginal vein and terminates in the right atrium. The coronary sinus functions to o collect deoxygenated blood from the myocardium of the heart and drain it into the right atrium.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Coronary sinus atrial septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An atrial septal defect characterized by a deficiency in the tissue separating the coronary sinus from the left atrium (LA). This results in partial or complete unroofing of the coronary sinus leading to a predominantly left-to-right shunt through the coronary sinus (LA to coronary sinus to right atrium [RA]). The orifice of the ostium is frequently large because of the increased flow. From the RA side, the defect is located at the level of the coronary sinus ostium and may also include some deficiency in atrial tissue around the ostium. From the LA side, the size can be variable depending on the degree of unroofing of the coronary sinus. There is partial (either focal or fenestrated) or complete absence of the roof of the CS, which results in a communication between the CS and the LA. Unroofed CS is the rarest type of atrial septal defect. It is often associated with persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) and other forms of complex congenital heart disease, usually heterotaxia syndromes.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:18806021, PMID:19398672, PMID:40843896]"}

name: Coronary sinus diverticulum
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A venous pouch within the left ventricular wall, with a neck opening into the coronary sinus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:3138904]"}

name: Dilatation of the sinus of Valsalva
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation of one of the anatomic dilations of the ascending aorta, which occurs just above the aortic valve.\" []"}

name: Juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized at the insertion of the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the juxtaductal region of aortic arch.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Postductal coarctation of the aorta
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized distal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the postductal region of aortic arch.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus in postnatal life when birth was at 37 completed weeks of gestation or greater.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus when birth was at less than 37 weeks completed gestation.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Bilateral ductus arteriosus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of both a left and a right ductus arteriosus.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:6193702]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventritricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:6193702]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, and also has a pulmonary stenosis; abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:10431853]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, but there is not accompanying pulmonary stenosis; the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:10431853]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:6193702]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:6193702]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:6193702]"}

name: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.\" [PMID:20069085, PMID:6193702]"}

name: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Features of tetralogy of Fallot with either rudimentary ridges or the complete absence of pulmonic valve tissue.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the ascending aorta with the contralateral pulmonary artery arising from the right ventricle.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:2590592]"}

name: Anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The left pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Tricuspid atresia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Failure to develop of the tricuspid valve and thus lack of the normal connection between the right atrium and the right ventricle.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Right ventricular cardiomyopathy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Right ventricular dysfunction (global or regional) with functional and morphological right ventricular abnormalities, with or without left ventricular disease.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17916581]"}

name: Left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is characterized by prominent left ventricular trabeculae and deep inter-trabecular recesses. The myocardial wall is often thickened with a thin, compacted epicardial layer and a thickened endocardial layer. In some patients, LVNC is associated with left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction, which can be transient in neonates.\" [PMID:17916581]"}

name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Transient left ventricular apical ballooning syndrome or takotsubo cardiomyopathy is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction involving the left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease on coronary angiography. Patients present with an abrupt onset of angina-like chest pain, and have diffuse T-wave inversion, sometimes preceded by ST-segment elevation, and mild cardiac enzyme elevation.\" [PMID:17916581]"}

name: Absent right superior vena cava
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of the right superior vena cava (RSVC). An absent RSVC is always associated with a persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC). During normal fetal development, the left-sided anterior venous cardinal system regresses, leaving the coronary sinus (CS) and the ligament of Marshall. Failure of the closure of the left anterior cardinal vein results in PLSVC. In general, PLSVC is associated with the right superior vena cava (RSVC) and drains into the RA via a dilated CS. When developmental arrest occurs at an earlier stage, the CS is absent and the PLSVC drains into the left atrium.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:17578953, PMID:19808620, PMID:20532458]"}

name: Bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein
Bilateral superior vena cava with no bridging vein
Left superior vena cava draining directly to the left atrium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the left atrium instead of the right atrium via the coronary sinus, resulting in a right to left sided shunt.\" [PMID:18847480]"}

name: Left superior vena cava draining to coronary sinus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the right atrium via the coronary sinus. This is the case in 80-92% of cases of PLSVC and results in no hemodynamic consequence.\" [PMID:18847480]"}

name: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation is the result of connection failure between the right subcardinal vein and the right vitelline vein. Consequently, venous blood from the caudal part of the body reaches the heart via the azygous vein and superior vena cava.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:10550884]"}

name: Cardiac myxoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) of the heart. Cardiac myxomas consist of stellate to plump, cytologically bland mesenchymal cells set in a myxoid stroma. Cardiac myxomas are of endocardial origin and general project from the endocardium into a cardiac chamber.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:7477198]"}

name: Cardiac hemangioma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal proliferation of blood vessels within the cardiac cavities attached to the endocardium.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Cardiac teratoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A teratoma within the heart. Most commonly, these tumors are detected in the pericardial cavity attached to the pulmonary artery and aorta. The tumor size within the heart varies from 2 to 9 cm in diameter, and intrapericardial tumors as large as 15 cm have been reported. Intracardiac tumors arise from the atrial or ventricular wall as nodular masses protruding into the cardiac chambers. Cardiac and pericardial teratomas are easily detected in the fetus and neonate by two-dimensional echocardiography as heterogeneous and encapsulated cystic masses. Histologically, cardiac teratomas contain multiple immature elements including epithelium, neuroglial tissue, thyroid, pancreas, smooth and skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17331235]"}

name: Arrhythmia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:19063792]"}

name: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent subarterial conus
Tetralogy of Fallot with atrioventricular canal defect
Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia in which all pulmonary blood flow is derived from major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (MAPCA).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:22368654]"}

name: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary stenosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The commonest form of tetralogy of Fallot characterized by pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy, without pulmonary atresia, absent pulmonary valve, atrioventricular canal defect or absent subarterial conus.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Subarterial ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A ventricular septal defect that lies beneath the semilunar valve(s) in the conal or outlet septum.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:10798413]"}

name: Perimembranous ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A ventricular septal defect that is confluent with and involves the membranous septum and is bordered by an atrioventricular valve, not including the type 3 VSDs.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:10798413]"}

name: Restrictive ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that is small enough to restrict flow across it such that a pressure gradient exists between the two sides of the VSD.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:10798413]"}

name: Non-restrictive ventricular septal defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that does not restrict flow across it sufficiently to generate a pressure gradient between the two sides of the VSD.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Infra-aortic superior vena cava
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The superior vena cava passes below the aortic arch.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Abnormal coronary artery course
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal path of a coronary artery.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: AV nodal tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of supraventricular tachycardia that originates in the atrioventricular node.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, PMID:20733110]"}

name: Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Supraventricular tachycardia in which an accessory pathway connecting the atria and ventricles, apart from the AV node, participates as a necessary part of a reentrant mechanism.\" [PMID:22459483]"}

name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway that is called concealed because it is not seen on the ECG during sinus rhythm.\" [PMID:22459483]"}

name: Permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An incessant orthodromic tachycardia with anterograde conduction over the atrioventricular node and by retrograde conduction via an accessory pathway usually located in the posteroseptal region with slow and decremental conduction.\" [PMID:15831598]"}

name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the left free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the right free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the septum
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway
Cerebellar hemorrhage
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Hemorrhage into the parenchyma of the cerebellum.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the left free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the right free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the septum
Automatic atrial tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Chronic supraventricular tachycardia predominantly seen in childhood.\" [PMID:4019927]"}

name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Multifocal atrial tachycardia is a rare supraventricular arrhythmia in neonates and young infants that is characterized by multiple P waves with varying P wave morphology and is usually asymptomatic.\" [ORPHA:3282]"}

name: Abnormal electrophysiology of sinoatrial node origin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium. THe SA node acts as the pacemaker of the heart.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Sinus tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Heart rate of greater than 100 beats per minute.\" []"}

name: Sick sinus syndrome
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality involving the generation of the action potential by the sinus node and is characterized by an atrial rate inappropriate for physiological requirements. Manifestations include severe sinus bradycardia, sinus pauses or arrest, sinus node exit block, chronic atrial tachyarrhythmias, alternating periods of atrial bradyarrhythmias and tachyarrhythmias, and inappropriate responses of heart rate during exercise or stress.\" [PMID:17420362]"}

name: First degree atrioventricular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Delay of conduction through the atrioventricular node, which is manifested as prolongation of the PR interval in the electrocardiogram (EKG). All atrial impulses reach the ventricles.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Second degree atrioventricular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An intermittent atrioventricular block with failure of some atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, i.e., some but not all atrial impulses are conducted through the atrioventricular node and trigger ventricular contraction.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Mobitz I atrioventricular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Progressive PR interval prolongation with the subsequent occurrence of a single nonconducted P wave that results in a pause. The pause that follows the nonconducted impulse is less than fully compensatory (less than the sum of two normal sinus intervals).\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Mobitz II atrioventricular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of second degree atrioventricular (AV) block characterized by sudden failure to conduct an impulse through the AV node without a preceding change in the PR interval.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Atrioventricular dissociation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Atrioventricular (AV) dissociation is present if the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers. AV dissociation can occur in the absence of a primary AV conduction disturbance.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Bundle branch block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Block of conduction of electrical impulses along the Bundle of His or along one of its bundle branches.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Left anterior fascicular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Conduction block in the anterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Complete right bundle branch block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A conduction block of the right branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a prolongation of the QRS complex (greater than 0.12 s) with delayed activation of the right ventricle and terminal delay on the EKG.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Left bundle branch block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A conduction block of the left branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a generalized disturbance of QRS morphology on EKG.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Libman-Sacks lesions
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Libman-Sacks valvular lesions are sterile fibrofibrinous vegetations that favor the left-sided heart valves and usually form on the ventricular surface of the mitral valve.\" [PMID:18421506]"}

name: Trifascicular block
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal conduction in all three divisions of the intraventricular conducting tissue.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Junctional ectopic tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is a unique type of supraventricular arrhythmia defined by narrow QRS complex and atrioventricular (AV) dissociation or retrograde atrial conduction in a 1:1 pattern.\" [PMID:22826742]"}

name: Atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Accessory pathway-related atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) involves an abnormal electrical conduction of the accessory pathway. The accessory pathway connecting impulses between the atrium and the ventricle can be seen at any site in the AV groove.\" []"}

name: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
Cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
Infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
Mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
Congenital malformation of the right heart
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the right heart identifiable at birth.\" []"}

name: Uhl's anomaly
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Uhl anomaly of the right ventricle refers to the almost complete absence of right ventricular myocardium, normal tricuspid valve, and preserved septal and left ventricular myocardium.\" [PMID:10859296, PMID:16322929]"}

name: Persistent fetal circulation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Systemic desaturation of a liveborn baby resulting from persistent pulmonary hypertension with a patent ductus arteriosus and patent foramen ovale, such that the circulation in postnatal life follows the fetal course.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]"}

name: Elbow clonus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Clonus at the elbow joint, i.e., an exaggerated phasic stretch reflex characterized by repetitive, rhythmic contractions at the elbow, generated by rapid passive stretch at the elbow joint.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormality of joint mobility
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality in the range and ease of motion of joints across their normal range.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal central sensory function
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of sensation related to CNS function. Assuming the primary sensory modalities are intact and the patient is alert and cooperative, the presence of an abnormality of sensory function may indicate a lesion of a parietal cortex, the thalamocortical projections to the parietal cortex, or the spinal cord.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormality of circulating cortisol level
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the concentration of cortisol in the blood.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal adrenal morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any structural anomaly of the adrenal glands.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormality of adrenal physiology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A functional abnormality of the adrenal glands.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Central adrenal insufficiency
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A form of adrenal insufficiency related to a lack of ACTH, which leads to a decrease in the production of cortisol by the adrenal glands. Aldosterone production is not usually affected.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Adrenocorticotropin deficient adrenal insufficiency
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in ACTH production.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by a defect within the adrenal gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Corticotropin-releasing hormone deficient adrenal insufficiency
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in corticotropin-releasing hormone production.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor defect
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Dexamethasone-suppressible primary hyperaldosteronism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone can be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Glucocortocoid-insensitive primary hyperaldosteronism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone cannot be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone or similar glucocorticoids.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Secondary hyperaldosteronism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by abnormally increased renin levels.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Ectopic adrenal gland
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal anatomical location of the adrenal gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Secondary hypercortisolism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Hypercortisolemia associated with a overproduction of ACTH (often from a tumor), leading secondarily to overproduction of cortisol.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Non-secretory adrenocortical adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An hormonally inactive adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that does not secrete excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Secretory adrenocortical adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An hormonally active adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that secretes excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Abnormality of the anterior pituitary
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A reduced ability to secrete adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), a hormone that stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete of glucocorticoids such as cortisol.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone excess
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Overproduction of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), which generally leads secondarily to overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Neoplasm of the anterior pituitary
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Abnormal posterior pituitary morphogenesis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Neoplasm of the posterior pituitary
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of a neoplasm (tumor) in the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Posterior pituitary dysgenesis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal development of the neurohypophysis during embryonic growth and development.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituicytoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A solid, low grade, spindle cell, glial neoplasm of adults that originates in the neurohypophysis or infundibulum. Clinical signs and symptoms include visual disturbance, headache and features of hypopituitarism. Pituicytomas are well-circumscribed, solid masses that can measure up to several centimeters. name: Ectopic posterior pituitary
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal anatomical location of the posterior lobe of the hypophysis, also known as the neurohypophysis. The posterior pituitary is normally present in the dorsal portion of the sella turcica, but when ectopic is usually near the median eminence. This defect is likely to be due to abnormal migration during embryogenesis.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Posterior pituitary agenesis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of the neurohypophysis owing to a developmental defect.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituitary gonadotropic cell adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of pituitary adenoma that produces gonadotropins.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituitary growth hormone cell adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of pituitary adenoma that produces growth hormone.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituitary null cell adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of pituitary adenoma that is of unknown cellular origin and that lacks immunocytochemical or fine structural markers. Null cell adenomas are not associated with hormone excess.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of pituitary adenoma that produces thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Pituitary carcinoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A pituitary tumor with subarachnoid, brain, or systemic metastasis. The diagnosis of a pituitary carcinoma requires evidence of metastatic disease, either outside the central nervous system (CNS) or as separate noncontiguous foci within the CNS.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, NCIT:C4536, PMID:15741248]"}

name: Pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A spindled-to-epithelioid, oncocytic, nonendocrine neoplasm of the anterior hypophysis that manifests in adults and follows a benign clinical course. Pituitary spindle cell oncocytomas are firm, fibrous, and adherent to surrounding structures and are highly vascular.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, PMID:21886889]"}

name: Abnormal parathyroid morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A structural abnormality of the parathyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A functional abnormality of the parathyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Parathyroid dysgenesis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal embryonic development of the parathyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Ectopic parathyroid
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal anatomical location of the parathyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of hyperparathyroidism that occurs following kidney transplantation, which is a treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Although kidney transplantation leads to a normalization of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone in most patients. The state of persistent hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism is referred to as tertiary hyperparathyroidism.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of hypoparathyroidism with circulating antiparathyroid or anti-calcium sensing receptor antibodies indicative of autoimmunity.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, PMID:19328421]"}

name: Abnormal thyroid morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A structural abnormality of the thyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Uninodular goiter
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to a singular nodule in the thyroid gland.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Thyroid hemiagenesis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of a lobe of the thyroid gland related to a failure of its embryologic development.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547]"}

name: Thyroid C cell hyperplasia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal growth of parafollicular (C-cells) cells.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Thyrotoxicosis with toxic single thyroid nodule
Central hypothyroidism
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of hypothyroidism due to an insufficient stimulation of an otherwise normal thyroid gland. Central hypothyroidism is caused by either pituitary (secondary hypothyroidism) or hypothalamic (tertiary hypothyroidism) defects.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0538-4547, PMID:18415684]"}

name: Increased circulating free T3
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An elevated concentration of free 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the blood circulation.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid stimulating hormone
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Reduced sensitivity of thyroid follicle cells to stimulation by biologically active thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).\" [PMID:28648507]"}

name: Neoplasm by histology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Neoplasm categorized according to type of histological abnormality.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Neoplasm by anatomical site
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Neoplasm categorized according to the anatomical site of origin of the neoplasm.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Embryonal renal neoplasm
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of an embryonal neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Intralobar nephroblastomatosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Presence of persistent islands of renal blastema in the postnatal kidney, anywhere within a renal lobe (a portion of a kidney consisting of a renal pyramid and the renal cortex above it).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Perilobar nephroblastomatosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormally persistent foci of embryonal immature blastema located in the superficial cortical region (perilobar).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 1
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma that is characterized by small cuboidal cells covering thin papillae with a single line of uniform nuclei and small nucleoli.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978, PMID:12429790]"}

name: Renal oncocytoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A renal tumor originating from an oncocyte, which is an epithelial cell characterized by an excessive amount of mitochondria, resulting in an abundant acidophilic, granular cytoplasm.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9113-2978]"}

name: Midface retrusion
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Posterior positions and/or vertical shortening of the infraorbital and perialar regions, or increased concavity of the face and/or reduced nasolabial angle.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9602-2321, PMID:19125436]"}

name: Hamartoma of tongue
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the tongue.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17667541]"}

name: Bifid nose
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Visually assessable vertical indentation, cleft, or depression of the nasal bridge, ridge and tip.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Abnormal muscle physiology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A functional abnormality of a skeletal muscle.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal skeletal muscle morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A structural abnormality of a skeletal muscle.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Type 1 muscle fiber atrophy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Atrophy (wasting) affecting primary type 1 muscle fibers. This feature in general can only be observed on muscle biopsy.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Decreased patellar reflex
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Decreased intensity of the patellar reflex (also known as the knee jerk reflex).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Paradoxical myotonia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of myotonia that worsens with repeated muscle contractions.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:7678441]"}

name: Impaired two-point discrimination
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A reduced ability to distinguish tactile sensations at points that are very close to one another. This can be tested by using special calipers whose points can be set from 2mm to several centimeters apart.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Impaired touch localization
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A reduced ability to identify precisely the site of a touch. This test is usually carried out by asking a patient, whose eyes are closed or covered, to touch the same site with a fingertip.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Agraphesthesia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Impaired ability to recognize letters or numbers drawn by an examiner's fingertip on the patient's skin (the patients eyes are closed or covered throughout this examination).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Increased cerebral lipofuscin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Lipofuscin (age pigment) is a brown-yellow, electron-dense, autofluorescent material that accumulates progressively over time in lysosomes of postmitotic cells, such as neurons and cardiac myocytes. This term pertains if there is an increase in the accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:9531959]"}

name: Increased urinary hypoxanthine level
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The concentration of hypoxanthine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Cephalocele
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital defect in the skull, whereby there is a protrusion of part of the cranial contents through a congenital defect in the cranium, usually covered with skin or mucous membrane. The term encephalocele refers to a subclass of these lesions in which brain tissue protrudes through the defect.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:24931720]"}

name: Parietal encephalocele
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An encephalocele located between bregma and lambda.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2972-5481, PMID:2773494]"}

name: Basal encephalocele
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Basal encephalocele is an encephalocele that occurs along the cribriform plate or through the sphenoid bone. The mass may appear in the nasal cavity, nasopharynx, epipharynx, sphenoid sinus, posterior orbit, or pterygopalatine fossa. The important distinction from other types is that no external tumor is visible except in those rare instances of herniations so large that they protrude through the mouth or nares.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:4966739]"}

name: Submucous cleft soft palate
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A cleft of the muscular (soft) portion of the palate that is covered by mucous membrane. Soft-palate submucous clefts are characterized by a midline deficiency or lack of muscle tissue.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Membranous choanal atresia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of the normal opening of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture) as a result of an obstructing choanal membrane that may be thin and strandlike or thick and pluglike.\" [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_jhurst]"}

name: Abnormal facial skeleton morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of one or more of the set of bones that make up the facial skeleton.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2972-5481]"}

name: Broad chin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Increased width of the midpoint of the mandible (mental protuberance) and overlying soft tissue.\" [PMID:19125436]"}

name: Chin with horizontal crease
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Horizontal crease or fold situated below the vermilion border of the lower lip and above the fatty pad of the chin, with the face at rest.\" [PMID:19125436]"}

name: Chin with H-shaped crease
extra_json: {"definition": "\"H-shaped crease in the fat pad of the chin.\" [PMID:19125436, PMID:20012803]"}

name: Tented philtrum
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Prominence of a triangular soft tissue area of the philtrum with the apex to the columella.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Philtrum with midline raphe
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Narrow ridge in the midline of the philtral groove.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Malaligned philtral ridges

name: Midline sinus of philtrum
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pit in the midline of the philtral groove.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Narrow philtrum
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Distance between the philtral ridges, measured just above the vermilion border, more than 2 standard deviations below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between the ridges of the philtrum.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Deviated nasal tip
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Nasal tip positioned to one side of the midline.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Narrow nasal tip
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Decrease in width of the nasal tip.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Overhanging nasal tip
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Positioning of the nasal tip inferior to the nasal base.\" [PMID:19152422]"}

name: Moyamoya phenomenon
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A noninflammatory, progressive occlusion of the intracranial carotid arteries owing to the formation of netlike collateral arteries arising from the circle of Willis.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Delayed talus ossification
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Delayed maturation and calcification of the talus.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Sclerodactyly
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Localized thickening and tightness of the skin of the fingers or toes.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal total T cell number
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number (either count per volume or proportion of total lymphocytes) of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:22420532]"}

name: Ventricular flutter
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia characterized by an extremely rapid, hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia (150-300 beats/min) with a large oscillating sine-wave appearance.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal skeletal morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the form, structure, or size of the skeletal system.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal musculoskeletal physiology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormality of the function of the skeletal system.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal appendicular skeleton morphology

name: Osteoblastoma

name: Giant cell tumor of bone

name: Abdominal colic

name: Abnormal bone ossification
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any anomaly in the formation of bone or of a bony substance, or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:18157903]"}

name: Hemopericardium
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Accumulation of blood within the pericardial sac.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:10882282]"}

name: Chylopericardium

name: Serous pericardial effusion

name: Pica
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An appetite for and the persistent ingestion of non-food substances such as clay. In order to diagnose pica, this behavior must have persisted over a period of at least one month.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Plasmacytoma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A discrete mass of neoplastic monoclonal plasma cells either in the bone marrow or in an extramedullary location.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Reduced factor IX activity

name: Punctate keratitis

extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of spots or rounded patches of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Abnormal bone collagen fibril morphology

name: Abnormal iliac wing morphology

name: Abnormal platelet function
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any anomaly in the function of thrombocytes.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal response to arachidonic acid as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of arachidonic acid.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790]"}

name: Impaired thrombin-induced platelet aggregation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Abnormal response to thrombin or thrombin mimetics as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of thrombin (or thrombin mimetics).\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790]"}

name: Abnormal platelet count

name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Low platelet count following administration of unfractionated or (less commonly) low-molecular weight heparin.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:16928996]"}

name: Abnormal platelet morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An anomaly in platelet form, ultrastructure, or intracellular organelles.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4381-2442]"}

name: Abnormal platelet volume
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anomalous size of platelets. Most normal sized platelets are 1.5 to 3 micrometers in diameter. Large platelets are 4 to 7 micrometers. Giant platelets are larger than 7 micrometers and usually 10 to 20 micrometers.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Increased mean platelet volume
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Average platelet volume above the upper limit of the normal reference interval.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790]"}

extra_json: {"definition": "\"Presence of reduced amount of a membrane protein on the cell membrane of platelets. This feature is typically measured by flow cytometry.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790]"}

name: Decreased platelet glycoprotein Ib-IX-V

name: Acute disseminated intravascular coagulation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An acute form of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Acute DIC can occur following sudden exposure of blood to procoagulants, with the compensatory hemostatic mechanisms becoming overwhelmed.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]"}

name: Decreased platelet glycoprotein VI

name: Decreased platelet P2Y12 receptor
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Decreased cell membrane concentration of P2Y12 receptor.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790, PMID:14755328]"}

name: Abnormal platelet granules
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An anomaly of alpha or dense granules or platelet lysosomes.\" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7744-1790, PMID:18041654]"}
