name: Poor R-wave progression
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of the normal increase in size of the R wave in the precordial leads when advancing from lead V1 to V6 of the electrocardiogram.\" [PMID:35181482]"}

name: Prominent V1-V2 R wave
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The R wave in leads V1-V2 is normally considerably smaller in amplitude than the S wave in the same leads. Prominent R wave in these leads implies the R wave is larger than the S-wave, which may indicate cardiovascular pathology. This term includes Tall R wave in lead V1, which is defined by a R/S ratio greater than 1.\" [PMID:11593472]"}

name: Finger mass
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a finger.\" []"}

name: Foot mass
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a foot.\" []"}

name: Abnormal retinal vein morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by structural abnormalities of the retinal veins, including tortuosity, dilation, narrowing, or irregularities in branching patterns. These changes may be associated with systemic or ocular diseases such as retinal vein occlusion, diabetic retinopathy, or hypertensive retinopathy.\" []"}

name: Spongiosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Spongiosis refers to the increased intercellular edema in the epidermis resulting in the pulling away of the keratinocytes from their surrounding desmosomes. Histologically, the spongiotic tissue reaction pattern involves the accumulation of fluid in the intercellular spaces of the epidermis, making the desmosomes junctions more easy to appreciate. Parakeratosis forms above the areas of spongiosis. The foci of spongiosis can be microscopic to grossly identifiable clinically with vesicles or bullae.\" [PMID:28237387, PMID:37445645]"}

name: Discoid adrenal gland
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A congenital finding where the adrenal gland does not form it's typical triangular, Y or V shape and is instead discoid, straight or elongated in shape. It is often found incidentally on renal ultrasound and is associated with renal agenesis and other renal congenital anomalies.\" [PMID:33552228]"}

name: Abnormal optic disc vasculature morphology
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A structural abnormality in the blood vessels of the optic disc, including bleeding, tortuosity, dilation, shunting, or other unusual branching patterns.\" []"}

name: Supraclavicular nerve distribution
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Localization of symptoms such as numbness or paresthesias on the skin over the upper chest, specifically above the clavicle and over the lateral aspect of the neck, corresponding to the distribution of the supraclavicular nerve.\" []"}

name: Limited shoulder internal rotation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm towards the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.\" []"}

name: Superior displacement of the humeral head
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An anterior posterior (AP) shoulder radiograph shows distance between the the proximal aspect of the humeral head and inferior aspect of the acromion of less than 7 mm.\" [PMID:8816337]"}

name: Increased compartment pressure
extra_json: {"definition": "\"intracompartmental pressure (ICP) over 30 mmHg. Acute compartment syndrome occurs when there is increased pressure within a closed osteofascial compartment, resulting in impaired local circulation. Acute compartment syndrome is considered a surgical emergency since, without proper treatment, it can lead to ischemia and eventually necrosis. Generally, acute compartment syndrome is considered a clinical diagnosis. However, ICP over 30 mmHg can be used as a threshold to aid in diagnosis.\" [PMID:28846257]"}

name: Pain at the lateral aspect of the elbow
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pain localized to the radial aspect of the elbow.\" []"}

name: Pain at the posterior aspect of the elbow
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pain localized to the posterior aspect of the elbow.\" []"}

name: Pain at the medial aspect of the elbow
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pain localized to the medial aspect of the elbow.\" []"}

name: Radial nerve distribution
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Applies to the localization of findings corresponding to the distribution of the radial nevrve, such as (i)paresthesias on the dorsoradial aspect of the hand and wrist, including the dorsal thumb, index finger and middle finger and (ii) Weakness in elbow extension, wrist extension, finger extension, thumb extension and/or supination of the forearm.\" []"}

name: Omovertebral bone
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An osseous connection between the superomedial border of the right scapula and C5-C6 spinous processes.\" [PMID:38908946]"}

name: Clavicular edema
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Swelling on the chest between the neck and the shoulder, above the clavicel (collar bone).\" []"}

name: Positive CSF anti-measles antibody test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of measles virus.\" [PMID:30680706, PMID:32809508]"}

name: Vogt striae
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Vertical lines in the posterior stroma of the cornea, aligned with Descemet membrane. These lines temporarily disappear with pressure applied to the cornea. Vogt striae are a hallmark feature of keratoconus but have also been observed in healthy eyes. Rare cases of horizontal striae have been reported.\" [PMID:18700919]"}

name: Choroid thickening
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the thickness of the choroid, which may be associated with various ocular or systemic conditions. Choroid thickening can be measured using imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT).\" [PMID:39095470]"}

name: Corneal epithelial edema
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by accumulation of fluid within the corneal epithelium, leading to swelling, blurred vision, and discomfort. It is often associated with increased intraocular pressure, endothelial dysfunction, or contact lens overuse. Clinical features may include a hazy cornea and microcystic changes visible on slit-lamp examination.\" []"}

name: Retinal shunt vessels
extra_json: {"definition": "\"bnormal blood vessels in the retina that form as a response to vascular occlusion, serving as bypass channels to redirect blood flow around obstructed or damaged retinal vessels. Retinal shunt vessels are often associated with conditions like retinal vein occlusion or diabetic retinopathy and may appear as tortuous or dilated vessels on fundoscopic examination.\" [PMID:37238303]"}

name: Filamentary keratitis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by the formation of filaments composed of degenerated epithelial cells and mucus attached to the corneal surface. It is associated with symptoms such as pain, foreign body sensation, photophobia, and tearing. Filamentary keratitis is often linked to underlying conditions such as dry eye disease, post-surgical ocular surface disorders, or systemic diseases like Sjoegren syndrome.\" [PMID:38857689]"}

name: Elevated circulating glucosylsphingosine concentration
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Concentration of D-glucosylsphingosine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.\" [PMID:39881421]"}

name: Optic disc hemorrhage
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by bleeding at or near the optic disc, visible as a flame-shaped or splinter hemorrhage on fundoscopic examination.\" [PMID:29217027]"}

name: Decreased circulating progranulin concentration
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The concentration of progranulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.\" []"}

name: Preauricular lymphadenopathy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Enlargement of one or more lymph nodes located in front of the ear.\" [PMID:32313895]"}

name: Onychoheterotopia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Growth of nail tissue outside the ungual plate, generally in the finger.\" [PMID:23716811, PMID:39641441]"}

name: Abnormal MHC surface expression
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A deviation from the normal level of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules expressed at the cell surface. The cell-mediated adaptive immune response is regulated by the MHC, which is called human leukocyte antigen (HLA) in humans. HLA molecules are cell surface glycoproteins whose primary function is to present endogenous and exogenous antigens to T lymphocytes for recognition and response. The HLA molecules that present antigen to T lymphocytes are divided into two main classes: HLA class I and HLA class II molecules.\" []"}

name: Forward displacement of posterior cervical dura mater on neck flexion
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Flexion MRI (imaging with neutral and flexed about 30-40 degrees neck position) reveals an anterior shift of the cervical dural sac from the lamina in the region of C4 to C7.\" [PMID:29763088, PMID:36475209]"}

name: Corneal dellen
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A localized area of corneal thinning typically occurring adjacent to an elevated lesion, such as a conjunctival scar, pterygium, or poorly fitting contact lens. Corneal dellen result from tear film instability and localized dehydration. Without timely treatment, they may progress to epithelial defects or corneal ulceration.\" [PMID:32596070]"}

name: Conjunctival xerosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by dryness of the conjunctiva, often associated with keratinization of the conjunctival epithelium. Conjunctival xerosis is commonly linked to vitamin A deficiency, severe dry eye disease, or systemic conditions such as Sjogren syndrome. Clinical features may include a dull, rough conjunctival surface and reduced mucosal secretions.\" [PMID:28939634]"}

name: Limited shoulder external rotation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.\" []"}

name: Occupational exposure to frequent hand trauma
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A history of exposure to repeated hand trauma as observed with occupations in which use of hands is frequent such as construction, food preparation and serving related occupations, and transportation and material moving occupations.\" []"}

name: Inability to fully extend finger at metacarpophalangeal joint
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An inability to fully extend the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of a finger (extension of an MCP joint straightens the finger).\" [PMID:39345665]"}

name: Scapholunate interval widening
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Widening of the space between the scaphoid and lunate on x-ray; scapholunate dissociation.\" [PMID:608295]"}

name: FInger pulp localization
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Applies to an abnormality whose distribution is limited to or predominantly affects the fleshy mass on the volar (palmar) aspect of the digit, distal to the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint (known as the pulp of the finger).\" []"}

name: Ulnar wrist pain
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the ulnar side of the wrist.\" []"}

name: Lunotriquetral interval widening
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Radiographic widening of the space between the lunate and triquetrum bones.\" []"}

name: Ulnar translocation of the carpus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Anteroposterior wrist radiograph showing ulnar translocation of the carpus from the distal radius with widening of the radial styloid-scaphoid space.\" [PMID:35415594]"}

name: Snapping sensation at time of injury
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A popping or snapping sensation (noise or feeling) at the time of an injury.\" []"}

name: Pagetoid spread
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pagetoid spread connotes the spread of single neoplastic cells, and small nests of them above the basal layer in a variety of melanocytic and nonmelanocytic neoplasms similar to the pattern seen in Paget's and in extramammary Paget disease.\" [PMID:20431478]"}

name: Scapholunate ligament tear
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the scapholunate ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Tear of the scapholunate ligament may lead to carpal instability.\" [PMID:32684689, PMID:38817761]"}

name: Lunotriquetral ligament tear
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the lunotriquetral ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Rupture or tear of the the lunotriquetral ligament may lead to carpal instability.\" [PMID:36689137]"}

name: Pisotriquetral arthritis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint. Radiographic evidence of arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint includes joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral cysts, and/or subchondral sclerosis.\" [PMID:27777815]"}

name: Volar intercalated segment instability
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of carpal instability characterized by volar tilt of the lunate bone.\" [PMID:32491661]"}

name: Inaccurate finger pulse oximetry oxygen saturation measurement
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Any substantial discrepancy between the measurement of oxygen saturation with finger probe pulse oximetry as compared to an arterial blood gas, which is considered the gold standard.\" [PMID:34652479]"}

name: Finger pulse oximetry lower than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Inaccurately reduced oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.\" [PMID:38340159]"}

name: Finger pulse oximetry higher than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Inaccurately elevated oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.\" [PMID:9792574]"}

name: History of thumb sucking past the age of four years
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Thumb sucking is a behavior that ceases spontaneously in most children between 2 and 4 years of age. If thumb sucking continues, negative consequences can occur, such as a deformity of the nail or paronychia. This term refers to a history of habitual thumb sucking past the age of 4 years of life.\" [PMID:32310572]"}

name: Cutaneous granulomatosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Skin inflammatory reaction triggered by a wide variety of stimuli, including infections, foreign bodies, malignancy, metabolites, and chemicals. From a pathogenic point of view, they are divided into non-infectious and infectious granulomas. From a clinical point of view, it is useful to divide cutaneous granulomatosis into localized and more disseminated forms, although this distinction can be sometimes artificial.\" [PMID:29352388]"}

name: Ureteric stricture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Obstruction of urine flow through one or both ureters caused by issues such as injury, infection, tumours and surgery.\" [PMID:25100183]"}

name: Arteriovenous crossing sign
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A retinal vascular abnormality characterized by indentation or compression of a retinal vein at an arteriovenous crossing, leading to changes in venous caliber. AV crossing signs are commonly associated with hypertensive retinopathy and may contribute to retinal vein occlusion. They are indicative of vascular remodeling due to chronic hypertension or other systemic vascular diseases.\" []"}

name: Haab striae
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Curvilinear or circumferential breaks in Descemet membrane, typically associated with congenital glaucoma. Haab striae result from elevated intraocular pressure during corneal development, leading to the formation of horizontal or arcuate lines that may be visible on slit-lamp examination. They can contribute to corneal astigmatism and visual impairment.\" [PMID:27993263, PMID:30554872]"}

name: Positive Legionella sputum culture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Growth of Legionella bacteria in a sputum culture.\" [PMID:38501659]"}

name: Positive Blastomyces dermatitidis sputum fungal stain
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Demonstration of Blastomyces dermatitidis by microscopic examination of a stained sputum specimen.\" [PMID:28723016]"}

name: Posterior shoulder pain
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the posterior (back) part of the shoulder.\" []"}

name: Superior shoulder pain
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the superior or proximal aspect of the shoulder over the acromion, distal clavicle, and/or acromioclavicular (AC) joint.\" []"}

name: Lateral shoulder pain
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the localized aspect (on the side) of the shoulder.\" []"}

name: Shoulder instability
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the shoulder with movement, shoulder 'giving way', or sensation of shoulder dislocating.\" []"}

name: Shoulder labrum tear
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A injury with a team (rip, split, or disruption) to the labrum, which is the ring of cartilage that surrounds the socket of the shoulder joint (the glenoid).\" []"}

name: Positive modified dynamic labral shear test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Sensation of a pain with or without clicking or clunking sensation with the following test. Flex patients elbow to 90 degrees and abduct the arm 120 degrees while maximally externally rotating the arm, then examiner lowers the arm to 60 degrees of abduction. A positive test occurs with pain and/or a painful click along the posterior joint line between 120 degrees and 90 degrees of abduction.\" [PMID:19509414]"}

name: Positive O'Brien active compression test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pain in shoulder reproduced when examiner applies downward pressure on the arm while patient resists pressure in the following position: elbow extended, shoulder forward flexed to 90 degrees and 10-15 degrees adducted with palm facing down. This can be compared to the same position but with the palm facing up which should be less painful.\" [PMID:17936025]"}

name: Positive shoulder apprehension test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The individual being investigated displays noticeable apprehension (unease) during a test for shoulder instability in which the individual is laying supine with shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 90 degrees, and an external rotation pressure with combined downward pressure is applied on the upper arm.\" [PMID:14977651]"}

name: Foamy tear film
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by the presence of foam or bubbles within the tear film, often associated with meibomian gland dysfunction or ocular surface diseases.\" [PMID:35508212]"}

name: Salzmann corneal nodules
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The formation of large, bluish, nodular lesions in the superficial corneal stroma, often associated with chronic keratitis or aging. These nodules may lead to visual impairment.\" [PMID:22228492]"}

name: Corneal stromal vascularisation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The abnormal growth of blood vessels into the corneal stroma, often associated with ocular herpes, chronic inflammation, infection, or hypoxia. This condition can lead to corneal scarring and vision impairment.\" []"}

name: Corneal iron line
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Linear or arcuate deposition of iron within the corneal epithelium or stroma, typically associated with conditions such as keratoconus, corneal degeneration, or postsurgical corneal changes.\" [PMID:21599747]"}

name: Conjunctivochalasis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by redundant, loose conjunctival tissue, typically located between the globe and the lower eyelid, which may cause ocular discomfort, tear film instability, or epiphora.\" []"}

name: Conjunctival hyperpigmentation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Increased pigmentation of the conjunctiva, characterized by brown or black discoloration due to melanocytic proliferation or pigment deposition. It may be associated with benign conditions such as primary acquired melanosis or malignant transformation into conjunctival melanoma.\" [PMID:34424954]"}

name: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Antibodies against antigens presented by the cell wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.\" [PMID:3143445]"}

name: Elevated fraction exhaled nitric oxide
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is elevated above the upper limit of normal. FeNO is an endogenous gaseous molecule which can be measured in the human breath test because of airway inflammation. It has been studied extensively as a marker of inflammation and has been incorporated into an algorithm for asthma management.\" [PMID:31417809]"}

name: Iris hyperemia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A condition characterized by increased blood flow and congestion of the iris vasculature, leading to a reddish discoloration of the iris. Iris hyperemia is commonly associated with anterior uveitis, angle-closure glaucoma, or ocular inflammation.\" []"}

name: Elevated circulating reticulated platelet count
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is above the upper limit of normal.\" [PMID:24807169]"}

name: Reduced circulating reticulated platelet count
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is below the lower limit of normal.\" [PMID:24807169]"}

name: Abnormal circulating reticulated platelet count
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is outside the limits of normal.\" [PMID:24807169]"}

name: Flexed posturing of finger
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A sign that can be observed in diseases such as Pyogenic or suppurative flexor tenosynovitis in which the affected finger is held in a flexed position. Often, there is pain on any attempt at passive finger extension. This finding is to be distinguished from a contracture of a finger joint in which the flexed positions is fixed.\" [PMID:35015439]"}

name: Positive synovial fluid alpha-defensin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Elevation of the the alpha-defensin concentration in synovial aspirate is above the upper limit of normal. The alpha-defensin test is a qualitative immunoassay optimized and validated for synovial fluid. The alpha-defensin protein is an antimicrobial peptide that is naturally released by neutrophils responding to a pathogen in the synovial fluid.\" [PMID:25631170]"}

name: Physeal fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Salter-Harris fractures (physeal fractures) refer to fractures through a growth plate (physis) and are, therefore, specifically applied to bone fractures in children.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Salter I fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture line extends through the physis or within the growth plate. Type I fractures are due to the longitudinal force applied through the physis, which splits the epiphysis from the metaphysis.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Salter II fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture extends through both the physis and metaphysis. These are most common and occur away from the joint space. When the small corner of the metaphysis is visible, this is known as a corner sign or Thurston-Holland fragment.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Salter III fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and extends from the physis into the epiphysis.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Salter IV fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and passes through the epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Salter V fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture that is due to a crush or compression injury of the growth plate. In type V, the force is transmitted through the epiphysis and physis, potentially disrupting the germinal matrix, hypertrophic region, and vascular supply.\" [PMID:28613461]"}

name: Nail bed laceration
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A cut or injury to the soft tissue under the fingernail or toenail.\" [PMID:34633779]"}

name: History of distal radius fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Recent or remote history of distal radius fracture of the symptomatic arm.\" []"}

name: History of triangular fibrocartilage complex tear
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Recent or remote history of a tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). The TFCC is a load-bearing structure between the lunate, triquetrum, and ulnar head. The function of the TFCC is to act as a stabilizer for the ulnar aspect of the wrist. The TFCC is at risk for either acute or chronic degenerative injury.\" [PMID:30725740]"}

name: Reduced plantar creases
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The creases (wrinkles) on the soles of the feet are less pronounced than normal, or absent.\" [PMID:6869501]"}

name: Skin burn
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Damage to the skin and underlying tissues caused by an agents such as heat, chemicals, electricity, radiation, or friction, resulting in pain, redness, swelling, and sometimes blisters or charring.\" []"}

name: Elevanted carboxysterol concentration in cultured lymphoblasts
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The concentration of carboxysterols in lymphoblastoid cells cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium is below the lower limit of normal.\" [PMID:21290788]"}

name: Superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An anomaly that can be ascertained by iron-specific magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences such as gradient-echo (GRE) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system is a chronic condition due to persistent or repeated long-term bleeding into the subarachnoid space, leading to subpial hemosiderin deposition. Hemosiderin deposition on MRI is seen as a T2 hypointensity and preferentially outlines the cerebellum and brainstem surface.\" [PMID:38753899]"}

name: Cortical superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that most commonly occurs due to iron deposits in the superficial cortical layers following bleeding from leptomeningeal vessels, most often from cerebral amyloid angiopathy in patients aged 55 or older.\" [PMID:33860558, PMID:38753899]"}

name: Infratentorial superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that involves the cerebellum and brainstem, most commonly the superior vermis, quadrigeminal plate, and basal cerebral surfaces. Cerebellar atrophy, particularly the superior vermis and anterior cerebellar hemispheres, can also be seen on a computed tomography scan of the head. The MRI of the spinal cord may reveal myelomalacia, syringomyelia, owl-eyes, or snake-eyes signs. The most common etiology for classic or primary infratentorial superficial siderosis is spinal dural defects, often dural tears.\" [PMID:33860558, PMID:38753899]"}

name: Pulmonary hyperplasia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Pulmonary Hyperplasia is an absolute increase in the number of alveoli, which are mildly enlarged. Pulmonary hyperplasia has been also referred to as polyalveolar lobe and type 3 cystic adenomatoid malformation.\" [PMID:7747754]"}

name: Positive protozoan parasite CSF wet mount test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Demonstration of protozoan parasites in a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimen by microscopy.\" [PMID:19635883]"}

name: Gallbladder polyp
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A gallbladder (GB) polyp is a growth that projects from the lining of the inside wall of the gallbladder into the lumen of the GB. GB polyps are a common incidental sonographic finding, the vast majority of which are benign.\" [PMID:38411693]"}

name: Gallbladder polyposis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Multiple polyps arising from the gallbladder mucosal wall.\" [PMID:29262128]"}

name: Biceps tendon rupture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Discontinuity of the biceps tendon as observed by ultrasound or magnetic resonance (MR) imaging.\" [PMID:30020607]"}

name: Medial epicondyle apophysitis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Medial epicondyle apophysitis (MEA), also known as little league elbow, is an overuse injury prevalent among adolescent athletes whose sport involves repetitive overhand throwing, racket use, or other overhead arm motions. The medial epicondyle is a bony protrusion on the medial elbow with its own ossification center, separate from the main distal humeral physis, known as an apophysis. Medial epicondyle apophysitis occurs due to excessive and repetitive valgus stress placed on the apophysis before its closure. Over time, the repetitive strain results in a traction-type injury and may cause pathologic widening and inflammation of the apophysis or even an avulsion fracture.\" [PMID:34033354]"}

name: Thumb carpometacarpal subluxation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A partial (subluxation) loss of alignment at the base of the thumb, where the first metacarpal bone meets the trapezium bone of the wrist. Thumb radiographs showing carpometacarpal (CMC) joint space widening and/or incongruity of the joint space between thumb metacarpal bone and the trapezium bone.\" [PMID:33927510]"}

name: Localized to lower eyelid
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A descriptor indicating that a condition, lesion, or abnormality is confined to the lower eyelid. This localization may be relevant for various ocular conditions, including infections, structural abnormalities, or dermatological diseases affecting the lower eyelid region.\" [PMID:30616908, PMID:37777491]"}

name: Localized to eyelid
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Applies to an abnormality that is situated in an eyelid.\" []"}

name: Halo vision
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A visual phenomenon characterized by the perception of bright rings or halos surrounding light sources. Halo vision is often associated with optical irregularities such as corneal edema, cataracts, or intraocular lens complications. It may also occur in conditions affecting the tear film or due to the presence of glare from light scattering within the ocular media.\" [PMID:12499461]"}

name: Hematospermia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The presence of blood in the seminal fluid.\" []"}

name: Choledocholithiasis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Choledocholithiasis is the presence of stones within the common bile duct.\" [PMID:28722990]"}

name: Axillary nerve distribution
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Paresthesias on the lateral aspect of the shoulder and upper arm. Weakness in shoulder abduction (deltoid) and shoulder external rotation (teres minor).\" []"}

name: Pelvic ring fracture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"X-ray of the pelvis (AP, inlet, and outlet views) showing fracture of the pelvic ring, including iliac wing (ilium), superior or inferior pubic ramus, or ischium, and/or displacement of the pubic symphysis or sacroiliac joints.\" []"}

name: Scapulothoracic dissociation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An injury consisting of a laterally displaced scapula with separation of the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint, disruption of the ipsilateral subclavian vessels and brachial plexus, and an intact overlying skin.\" [PMID:31046412]"}

name: Pain exacerbated by weight bearing
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Refers to pain that is worse when the individual bears weight with the affected body part.\" []"}

name: Thumb sign
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The distal phalanx of the adducted thumb extends beyond the ulnar border of the palm (The thumb protrudes from the clenched fist).\" [PMID:7616992]"}

name: Tibialis anterior tendon rupture
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Partial or complete breakage (rupture) of the tibialis anterior tendon (TAT). The TAT is the principal dorsiflexor of the ankle joint and secondary invertor of the foot. It has important roles in the different stages of gait; in the swing phase, it concentrically dorsiflex the ankle for foot clearance and during plantarflexion of the ankle in the stance phase, it eccentrically contract to stabilize the ankle and prevent damage to the foot and ankle. Clinically, presentations in acute lacerations or direct trauma cases are straight forward, in chronic and atraumatic cases usually the symptoms at the time of TAT rupture are more subtle. Other manifestations include mild pain, localized mass, palpable gap, loss of strength, instability during gait, gait disturbances with forefoot dropping and stumbling and high stepping gait.\" [PMID:31501017]"}

name: Decreased circulating ADAMTS13 activity
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Activity of the enzyme von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease (ADAMTS13) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.\" [PMID:12637323, PMID:30208220]"}

name: Abnormal methacholine challenge test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal result of the methacholine challenge test, which is a bronchoprovocation technique used to evaluate airway hyperresponsiveness, particularly in patients with suspected asthma.\" [PMID:31613496]"}

name: Positive stool glutamate dehydrogenase test
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Detection of the presence of glutamate dehydrogenase produced by Clostridium difficile in a stool sample.\" [PMID:24145018, PMID:35634999]"}

name: Retrocorneal membrane
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A retrocorneal membrane is an abnormal, fibrous or cellular tissue layer that forms on the posterior surface of the cornea, typically on or adjacent to the Descemet membrane. It may result from trauma, surgery (e.g., penetrating keratoplasty), inflammation, or endothelial cell dysfunction, and can lead to visual impairment depending on its density and extent.\" [PMID:20579631]"}

name: Adrenal hemorrhage
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Adrenal hemorrhage is bleeding within the capsule of the adrenal gland.\" [PMID:36404284, PMID:38432745]"}

name: Optic nerve sheath dilatation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An abnormal increase in the diameter of the optic nerve sheath, typically due to elevated intracranial pressure or local pathology affecting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics. It can be detected via imaging modalities such as ultrasound or MRI and may be associated with papilledema, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, or optic nerve tumors.\" [PMID:39585390]"}

name: Right ventricular thrombus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A blood clot (thrombus) localized in the right ventricle.\" [PMID:38746065]"}

name: Severe Candida infection
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Candida. Severe manifestations include invasive candidiasis with hematogenous spread (candidaemia), hepatosplenic candidiasis, renal candidiasis, Candida endophthalmitis, and Candida endocarditis.\" []"}

name: Phrenic neuropathy
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A functional deficit of the phrenic nerve. Phrenic neuropathy (PhN) is a debilitating condition characterized by impairment of the diaphragm muscle, the primary inspiratory muscle. Diaphragm muscle ultrasound is a noninvasive tool that appears to offer both high sensitivity and specificity for diagnosis. Alternatively, electrodiagnostic studies can assess phrenic nerve health. PhN is commonly diagnosed via diaphragm muscle US or fluoroscopy (sniff test) with paradoxical or significantly decreased diaphragm muscle movement.\" [PMID:39205612]"}

name: Glomerular basement membrane subendothelial remodeling
extra_json: {"definition": "\"New glomerular basement membrane matrix formation under the endothelial cell.\" [PMID:32866505]"}

name: Glomerular endothelium swelling
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Enlargement of the glomerular endothelium (the innermost layer of the glomerular filtration barrier) causing capillary lumen narrowing and loss of fenetrations.\" [PMID:32866505]"}

name: Medullary collecting duct ectasia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Widening of the lumen of the lumen of the collecting ducts in the renal medulla.\" [PMID:30523303]"}

name: Corneal keloid
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A raised, opaque, and fibrous lesion on the cornea resembling a dermal keloid, typically composed of disorganized collagen and fibrovascular tissue. Corneal keloids can impair vision and are often secondary to trauma, surgery, or underlying congenital disorders.\" [PMID:35598901]"}

name: Podocytic mitochondrial proliferation
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An ultrastructural abnormality of the kidney glomeruli characterized by an excessive number or abnormal aggregation of mitochondria in podocytes.\" [PMID:28117207]"}

name: Elevated vitamin D metabolite ratio
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The ratio of 24,25(OH)2D to 25(OH)D (also known as vitamin D metabolite ratio or VMR) is above the upper limit of normal.\" [PMID:26501157, PMID:37220642]"}

name: Aggravated by vitamin D supplementation

name: Aggravated by sun exposure
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Applied to a sign or symptom that becomes worse with exposure to sunlight.\" [PMID:31188746]"}

name: Tubular accumulation of uromodulin
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Accumulation of uromodulin within renal tubular cells or lumina.\" [PMID:31488840]"}

name: Elevated stool reducing substances
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Elevated level of reducing substances in the feces. If carbohydrate malabsorption is suspected, a reducing substance should be investigated in the stool using the Benedict or Fehling test. The presence of reducing substances may indicate an abnormality in carbohydrate (e.g., sucrose, lactase) metabolism. The unabsorbed sugars in stool are measured as reducing substances.\" []"}

name: Osteochondral lesion of talus
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Osteochondral lesion of the talus (OLT) is an injury involving the articular cartilage and subchondral bone, defined as any damage involving both articular cartilage and subchondral bone of the talar dome. OLT can cause ankle joint pain and can sometimes lead to instability and manifest as an area of abnormal, damaged cartilage and bone on the top of the talus bone (the lower bone of the ankle joint).\" [PMID:30498800, PMID:34386361]"}

name: Mallet toe
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A mallet toe involves the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint [such that] the distal phalanx is flexed on the middle phalanx.\" [PMID:32211125]"}

name: Bunionette deformity
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The bunionette, or tailor's bunion, is a lateral prominence of the fifth metatarsal head. Most commonly, bunionettes are the result of a widened 4-5 intermetatarsal angle with associated varus of the metatarsophalangeal joint.\" [PMID:17478753]"}

name: Elevated CSF beta chorionic gonadotropin concentration
extra_json: {"definition": "\"The concentration of beta chorionic gonadotropin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.\" [PMID:11007160]"}

name: Pigment epithelium detachment
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Separation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) from the underlying Bruch membrane.\" [PMID:28280989]"}

name: Retinal gliosis
extra_json: {"definition": "\"A pathological condition characterized by the proliferation of glial cells in the retina, often occurring as a reactive response to injury, inflammation, or degenerative changes, and typically resulting in structural and functional alterations in the retina.\" [PMID:26175331]"}

name: Aphakia
extra_json: {"definition": "\"Absence of the crystalline lens in the eye, which may be congenital or acquired (e.g., following surgical removal of the lens for cataracts or trauma).\" []"}

name: Pain on thumb extension
extra_json: {"definition": "\"An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort that is triggered upon extension (straightening) of the thumb.\" []"}

name: Fractured lunate bone
